title: Roles across the three steps
objective: Assign roles for a partner-led Visioning workshop and subsequent DITL.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: A Blueprint works when everyone knows their job before the customer joins the call. This lesson describes the usual division of labor and how to make it explicit for each engagement.

items: **Account Executive (AE).** Owns account strategy, customer coordination, and sponsor alignment. The AE secures executive buy-in before Visioning, finalizes the stakeholder list, and sends the agenda. Glean's Blueprint template has the AE lead the Visioning conversation, with the SE adding technical questions.

**Solutions Engineer (SE).** Normally leads technical and workflow depth in Day-in-the-Life (DITL) sessions. The SE validates feasibility and data assumptions and advises on how many DITL sessions the scope needs.
**Joint AE and SE.** Executive Validation is a joint run-of-show with the decision-makers present.
**Business Value Consultant (BVC).** Provides value expertise when the engagement warrants it. A BVC can facilitate, review a complex model, or build the executive business case.
**Partner.** Can facilitate discovery, bring industry and departmental context, and contribute delivery insight to the roadmap.

blocks.x: Before each customer meeting, agree on these roles:

blocks.caption: Run-of-show roles
head: Role
Responsibility in the session
rows: Keeps time, steers toward outcomes, manages participation
Captures the use case log, quotes, metrics, and open questions
Answers or parks feasibility questions; never guesses
Probes for baselines, volumes, and business impact
Keeps the executive informed and books the decision meeting
Sends the recap and updates the mutual action plan

blocks.x: One person can fill more than one role, but no role should be left implicit.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: These are operating principles, not a universal contractual RACI. Agree the split for each deal, and don't assume a partner can authorize Glean resources or commercial terms.
The ideal state, and the real one

Glean's Blueprint training describes the ideal state as the AE and SE working together on every step, from Visioning through DITL to the executive readout. The training is also candid that SE capacity is sometimes tight, so an AE may run steps an SE ideally would. When that happens, the AE shouldn't answer technical feasibility questions on the spot. Park them for the SE, so the deal doesn't stall and nothing unverified is promised.
For partners, the same principle applies. Decide who owns each role before the session, and note who will answer the questions nobody in the room can.

blocks.title: Who leads each step
blocks.alt: Five cards showing typical ownership: the AE leads Visioning with SE support; the SE leads DITL workflow mapping; the AE and SE jointly lead Executive Validation; the Business Value Consultant supports complex value cases; and the partner assists, co-leads, or leads by agreement.

items.detail: Leads Visioning; owns the sponsor path
